11616-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.creator: Unknown
11616-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. of our native oxen, and is of a slaty grey on the body and head; with cream-coloured legs and dewlap, the latter exceedingly long and pendulous; very short horns directed upwards and outwards; and ears of great proportional magnitude, and so flexible and obedient to the animal's will as to be moved in all directions with the greatest facility.

arxiv-1503-08476.title: Guided Grammar Convergence
arxiv-1503-08476.creator: Vadim Zaytsev, vadim@grammarware.net
arxiv-1503-08476.description: Abstract Relating formal grammars is a hard problem that balances between language equivalence (which is known to be undecidable) and grammar identity (which is trivial). In this paper, we investigate several milestones between those two extremes and propose a methodology for inconsistency management in grammar engineering.

arxiv-2012-13100.title: Generalized Potential and Mathematical Principles of Nonlinear Analysis
arxiv-2012-13100.creator: Peng Yue
arxiv-2012-13100.description: Abstract In the past hundred years, chaos has always been a mystery to human beings, including the butterfly effect discovered in 1963 and the dissipative structure theory which won the chemistry Nobel Prize in 1977. So far, there is no quantitative mathematical-physical method to solve and analyze these problems.

arxiv-2103-14861.title: Continued Fractions, Quadratic Fields, and Factoring: Some Computational Aspects
arxiv-2103-14861.creator: Michele Elia
arxiv-2103-14861.description: Abstract Legendre discovered that the continued fraction expansion of N \sqrt{N} having odd period leads directly to an explicit representation of N N as the sum of two squares. In this vein, it was recently observed that the continued fraction expansion of N \sqrt{N} having even period directly produces a factor of composite N N .

arxiv-2105-13196.title: Spectral instability of peakons in the b b -family of the Camassa–Holm equations
arxiv-2105-13196.creator: Stéphane Lafortune, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky
arxiv-2105-13196.description: Abstract . We prove spectral instability of peakons in the b b -family of Camassa–Holm equations in L 2 ​ ( ℝ ) L^{2}(\mathbb{R}) that includes the integrable cases of b = 2 b=2 and b = 3 b=3 .

arxiv-2204-07366.title: ResT V2: Simpler, Faster and Stronger
arxiv-2204-07366.creator: Qing-Long Zhang, Yu-Bin Yang
arxiv-2204-07366.description: Abstract This paper proposes ResTv2, a simpler, faster, and stronger multi-scale vision Transformer for visual recognition. ResTv2 simplifies the EMSA structure in ResTv1 (i.e., eliminating the multi-head interaction part) and employs an upsample operation to reconstruct the lost medium- and high-frequency information caused by the downsampling operation.

arxiv-2303-17152.title: Mixed Autoencoder for Self-supervised Visual Representation Learning
arxiv-2303-17152.creator: Kai Chen, Zhili Liu, Lanqing Hong, Hang Xu, Zhenguo Li, Dit-Yan Yeung
arxiv-2303-17152.description: Abstract Masked Autoencoder (MAE) has demonstrated superior performance on various vision tasks via randomly masking image patches and reconstruction. However, effective data augmentation strategies for MAE still remain open questions, different from those in contrastive learning that serve as the most important part. This paper studies the prevailing mixing augmentation for MAE.

arxiv-2306-01389.title: Spectral gaps and Fourier dimension diam for self-conformal sets with overlaps Thanks: S.B. is supported by an EPSRC New Investigator Award (EP/W003880/1). T.S. is supported by the Academy of Finland via the project Quantum chaos of large and many body systems , grant Nos. 347365, 353738.
arxiv-2306-01389.creator: Simon Baker, Tuomas Sahlsten
arxiv-2306-01389.description: Abstract . We prove a uniform spectral gap for complex transfer operators near the critical line associated to overlapping C 2 C^{2} iterated function systems on the real line satisfying a Uniform Non-Integrability (UNI) condition. Our work extends that of Naud (2005) on spectral gaps for nonlinear Cantor sets to allow overlaps.

arxiv-2308-00991.title: Wall and chamber structure for a special biserial algebra coming from perverse sheaves on ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n}
arxiv-2308-00991.creator: Alessio Cipriani, Martina Lanini
arxiv-2308-00991.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alessio Cipriani, Martina Lanini. We describe the wall and chamber structure of a special biserial algebra whose module category is equivalent to the category of (middle) perverse sheaves on the complex projective space ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} . In particular, by the well-known classification of indecomposable modules for special biserial algebras, we deduce that the algebra of interest is of finite representation type and we provide an explicit description of the walls of the structure.

arxiv-2412-15087.title: Qualitative Estimates of Topological Entropy for Non-Monotone Contact Lax-Oleinik Semiflow Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author.
arxiv-2412-15087.creator: Wei Cheng, Jiahui Hong, Zhi-Xiang Zhu ∗
arxiv-2412-15087.description: Abstract . For the non-monotone Hamilton-Jacobi equations of contact type, the associated Lax-Oleinik semiflow ( T t , C ⁡ ( M ) ) (T_{t},C(M)) is expansive. In this paper, we provide qualitative estimates for both the lower and upper bounds of the topological entropy of the semiflow. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 35F21,37L05,37B40,49L25 1.

arxiv-2501-13884.title: Exploring Finetuned Audio-LLM on Heart Murmur Features
arxiv-2501-13884.creator: Adrian Florea, Xilin Jiang, Nima Mesgarani, Xiaofan Jiang
arxiv-2501-13884.description: Abstract . Large language models (LLMs) for audio have excelled in recognizing and analyzing human speech, music, and environmental sounds. However, their potential for understanding other types of sounds, particularly biomedical sounds, remains largely underexplored despite significant scientific interest. In this study, we focus on diagnosing cardiovascular diseases using phonocardiograms, i.e., heart sounds.

arxiv-2503-09908.title: Parallel Batch-Dynamic Maximal Matching with Constant Work per Update
arxiv-2503-09908.creator: Guy E. Blelloch, Andrew C. Brady
arxiv-2503-09908.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guy E. Blelloch, Andrew C. Brady. We present a work optimal algorithm for parallel fully batch-dynamic maximal matching against an oblivious adversary. It processes batches of updates (either insertions or deletions of edges) in constant expected amortized work per edge update, and in O ⁡ ( log 3 ⁡ m ) O(\log^{3}m) depth per batch whp, where m m is the maximum number of edges in the graph over time.

arxiv-2505-02330.title: On Trigonometric Interpolation and Its Applications
arxiv-2505-02330.creator: Xiaorong \surname Zou
arxiv-2505-02330.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiaorong \surname Zou. In this paper, we propose a new trigonometric interpolation algorithm and establish relevant convergent properties. The method adjusts an existing trigonometric interpolation algorithm such that it can better leverage Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to enhance efficiency.

arxiv-2508-03291.title: Investigation on deep learning-based galaxy image translation models
arxiv-2508-03291.creator: Hengxin Ruan (阮恒心), Qiufan Lin (林秋帆), Shupei Chen (陈树沛), Yang Wang (汪洋), Wei Zhang (张伟)
arxiv-2508-03291.description: Abstract Galaxy image translation refers to a process that maps galaxy images from a source domain to a target domain, which is an important application in galaxy physics and cosmology. With deep learning-based generative models, image translation has been performed for image generation, data quality enhancement, information extraction, and generalized for other tasks such as deblending and anomaly detection.

arxiv-2604-27009.creator: Ryan Rae-Cheng Wee, Josef Bruzzese

europmc-pmc544838.creator: Sørensen HP, Mortensen KK.
europmc-pmc544838.description: Pure, soluble and functional proteins are of high demand in modern biotechnology. Natural protein sources rarely meet the requirements for quantity, ease of isolation or price and hence recombinant technology is often the method of choice. Recombinant cell factories are...

pmc-11494804.title: Ultrastructural characterization of hippocampal inhibitory synapses under resting and stimulated conditions
pmc-11494804.creator: Jung-Hwa Tao-Cheng, Sandra Lara Moreira, Christine A Winters
pmc-11494804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The present study uses electron microscopy to document ultrastructural characteristics of hippocampal GABAergic inhibitory synapses under resting and stimulated conditions in three experimental systems. Synaptic profiles were sampled from stratum pyramidale and radiatum of the CA1 region from (1) perfusion fixed mouse brains, (2) immersion fixed rat organotypic slice cultures, and from (3) rat dissociated hippocampal cultures of mixed cell types.

pmc-11510762.title: Identification of New Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms Potentially Related to Small Ruminant Lentivirus Infection Susceptibility in Goats Based on Data Selected from High-Throughput Sequencing
pmc-11510762.creator: Magdalena Materniak-Kornas, Katarzyna Ropka-Molik, Katarzyna Piórkowska, Joanna Kowalik, Tomasz Szmatoła, Jacek Sikora, Aldona Kawęcka, Jacek Kuźmak, Maria Filippa Addis
pmc-11510762.description: Small ruminant lentivirus (SRLV) infections are spread in the flocks of sheep and goats all over the world, causing economic loss. Although only a fraction of infected animals develop disease symptoms, all of them may shed the virus, causing uncontrolled spread of the infection.

pmc-11526622.title: Prenatal metal exposures and kidney function in adolescence in Project Viva
pmc-11526622.creator: Natalie F Price, Pi-I D Lin, Andres Cardenas, Sheryl L Rifas-Shiman, Ami R Zota, Marie-France Hivert, Emily Oken, Izzuddin M Aris, Alison P Sanders
pmc-11526622.description: BackgroundThe developing kidney is vulnerable to prenatal environmental factors such as metal exposure, potentially altering the risk of later-life kidney dysfunction. This study examines the relationship between prenatal metal exposures, individually and as mixtures, and adolescent kidney function in Project Viva, a prospective longitudinal birth cohort in Massachusetts, USA.

pmc-12469524.title: Using Participatory Action Research to Enhance Physical Education Interventions for Promoting Active Lifestyles in Schools: A Study Design and Protocol
pmc-12469524.creator: Jorge Lizandra, Alexandra Valencia-Peris, Roberto Ferriz, Carmen Peiró-Velert
pmc-12469524.description: Promoting active lifestyles among adolescents is essential due to their short-, medium-, and long-term contributions to young people’s holistic development and overall health. Beyond physical well-being, Physical Education foster physical activity, autonomy, social connectedness, motivation and emotional well-being, thus constituting a key dimension of quality education.

pmc-12559670.title: Immunoglobulin treatment and clinical outcomes: data from the Ontario Immunoglobulin Treatment program multicenter case registry
pmc-12559670.creator: Sarah Shehadeh, Stephen Betschel, Donald William Cameron, Danny Hill, Susan Waserman, Juthaporn Cowan
pmc-12559670.description: Background:The therapeutic use of immunoglobulin (IG) is increasing and accounts for the largest expenditure in the Canadian Blood Services budget. However, more granular data on IG utilization is limited.Objective:To describe IG treatment indications, dosing characteristics, and clinical outcomes in patients enrolled in the Ontario IG Treatment (ONIT) program, a government-funded pilot clinical program with a case registry.

pmc-12763901.title: Causal effects of ferroptosis-related traits on ovarian dysfunction: insights from integrating genome-wide Mendelian randomization, DNA methylation, gene expression, and proteome
pmc-12763901.creator: Qun Zhou, Bangli Song, Huifang Li, Yibo He, Hualiang Zhang, Jing Guo, Minjuan Wu, Wenjun Chen
pmc-12763901.description: BackgroundFerroptosis has been implicated in the development of ovarian dysfunction; however, the underlying causal genetic mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, a multi-omics Mendelian randomization (MR) approach was applied to systematically investigate the causal effects of ferroptosis-related molecular traits on ovarian dysfunction.

pmc-13002449.title: Development of a culturally tailored medical nutrition therapy to improve dietary adherence in type 2 diabetes in Benin: an ORBIT model-based protocol
pmc-13002449.creator: Halimatou Alaofè, Abidemi Okechukwu, Waliou Amoussa Hounkpatin, Adaeze Oguegbu, Kelly Jackson, Edward John Bedrick, John Ehiri
pmc-13002449.description: BackgroundDietitian-led medical nutrition therapy (MNT) is an effective and cost-efficient strategy for improving dietary adherence and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, culturally adapted MNT interventions that account for local food systems, food security, and sociocultural eating practices remain scarce in African contexts.

pmc-13208225.title: Application of Dang Van Model Based on Critical Plane Approach for Rolling Contact Problems
pmc-13208225.creator: Paweł J. Romanowicz
pmc-13208225.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Analyses of rolling contact fatigue (RCF) problems require the use of multiaxial fatigue criteria, which take into account complex non-proportional stress conditions. One of the most often used criteria to analyse this phenomenon is the Dang Van criterion. However, this criterion is often criticised due to its overestimation of the influence of compressive stresses on fatigue strength, which leads to an underestimation of the equivalent fatigue stress.

pmc-13213742.title: Effects of different thermal processing methods on the flavor and precursor substances of the longissimus dorsi muscle in the “Duroc × Landrace × Yorkshire” ternary hybrid pigs
pmc-13213742.creator: Xinran Yuan, Jialing Tang, Yulin Zhang, Zhengfeng Fang, Yong Yang, Guoquan Han, Teng Hui
pmc-13213742.description: This study investigated the effects of boiling, frying, and roasting on flavor compounds and their precursors in the longissimus dorsi muscle of “Duroc × Landrace × Yorkshire” pigs. HS-SPME-GC–MS, electronic nose analysis, and multivariate statistical methods (PCA, PLS-DA, and PLS-R) were used to characterize changes in free fatty acids (FFAs), free amino acids (FAAs), reducing sugars, and volatile compounds.

pmc-13221501.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: pathogenesis and novel treatment options
pmc-13221501.creator: Ruizhe Ren, Xiao Liang, Xiyang Wei
pmc-13221501.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the recently introduced terminology superseding non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver condition globally. This multisystem disorder, driven by systemic insulin resistance (IR) and metabolic dysregulation, not only progresses to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but also substantially increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), and extrahepatic malignancies.

pmc-13264119.title: TET3 promotes preeclampsia by regulating PDK4-mediated glucose metabolism reprogramming in trophoblasts
pmc-13264119.creator: Xiaokang Deng, Yi Liu, Meilikang Li, Weichun Tang, Lingling Jiang, Juveria Rahman, Matthew Sagnelli, Hongtao Hu, Lizhou Sun, Qing Zuo, Dan Wu, Yetao Xu
pmc-13264119.description: SummaryExtra villous trophoblasts (EVTs) dysfunction impairing spiral artery remodeling (SAR) is a key preeclampsia (PE) factor. ScRNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses of preeclamptic placentas revealed the upregulation of TET3, a newly recognized regulator of epigenetic reprogramming. Untargeted metabolomics further associated TET3 with the trophoblast glucose metabolism.

pmc-13301081.title: Evaluation of esophageal injury after very high-power short-duration pulmonary vein isolation using late gadolinium enhancement MRI
pmc-13301081.creator: N Van Pouderoijen, E L C H Stokman, L H G A Hopman, M B M Hofman, M J Mulder, M J B Kemme, M J W Gotte, C P Allaart
pmc-13301081.description: BackgroundEsophageal injury is a recognized complication of radiofrequency (RF) ablation for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Very high-power, short-duration (vHPSD) ablation may mitigate this risk by creating shallower lesions through enhanced resistive heating and limited conductive spread, potentially minimizing the depth of tissue damage. However, the temporal evolution of esophageal injury following PVI using vHPSD remains poorly understood.

pmc-13404472.title: Analysis of Retracted Publications in the Diabetes Literature
pmc-13404472.creator: Somayeh Parvin, Mahshid Lotfi, Mohsen Nouri
pmc-13404472.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRetraction serves as a critical corrective mechanism in scientific publishing, preventing the spread of flawed or misleading data. This study aimed to systematically analyze the characteristics of retracted articles within the field of diabetes research, highlight potential vulnerabilities in the integrity of diabetes research, and address gaps in understanding the nature and implications of research misconduct in this crucial medical discipline.Methods This study aimed to analyze retracted publications in the field of diabetes published from 1978 to 2024 using the Web of

pmc-13461419.creator: Yi Liao, Yang Jia, Zhigang Yang, Linjun Xie, Shiyu Xiong, Yilei Wang, Xiangao Lei, Yingkun Guo, Rong Xu

pmc-13505241.title: Time from pre‐labor rupture of membrane at term to delivery in grand multiparous women
pmc-13505241.creator: Shai Ram, Michael Lavie, Roy Bitan, David Nadav Sabag, Dotan Madar, Anat Lavie, Yariv Yogev, Roza Berkovitz Shperling
pmc-13505241.description: ObjectiveThe effect of parity on labor progression following term pre‐labor rupture of membranes (PROM) has been described, but detailed patterns among grand multiparous women remain unclear. Traditional labor models show accelerated labor with increasing parity, yet few studies have specifically examined PROM latency distributions or heterogeneity within high‐parity groups.

pmc-13517112.title: Enhancing a Mid-Wave Infrared Fourier Transform Hyperspectral Imager for Explosions
pmc-13517112.creator: James T. Stofel, Kody A. Wilson, Martin Larivière-Bastien, Anthony L. Franz, Michael L. Dexter
pmc-13517112.description: Capturing reliable hyperspectral imager data at a meaningful frame rate for explosions and other fast-changing scenes is not possible in the mid-wave infrared region under traditional sensor operating configurations and processing techniques, which typically have frame rates on the order of 0.5–2.0 Hz.

pmc-13585689.title: Parathyroid hormone–related protein–mediated hypercalcemia of malignancy: insights from a multicenter clinical data warehouse
pmc-13585689.creator: Jinyoung Kim, Yuri Shin, Jeonghoon Ha, Chaiho Jeong, Jeongmin Lee, Kwanhoon Jo, Jang Won Son, Jae-Seung Yun, Ihnsuk Lee, Dong-Jun Lim, Hyuk-Sang Kwon, Ki-Ho Song, Ki-Hyun Baek
pmc-13585689.description: Background/AimsParathyroid hormone–related protein (PTHrP) is a major mediator of hypercalcemia in patients with malignancy; however, understanding of PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia remains limited because available evidence has largely been derived from small case series.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed electronic medical records from eight hospitals affiliated with The Catholic University of Korea. Adult patients (> 20 years) with confirmed malignancy and albumin-corrected hypercalcemia (≥ 10.

pmc-13629000.title: A Walker and Avant concept analysis of slow code practice in end-of-life resuscitation
pmc-13629000.creator: Hamed gholizad gougjehyaran, Hadi Hassankhani, Elnaz Asghari, Hamidreza Haririan
pmc-13629000.description: BackgroundThe slow code is a complex and ethically sensitive phenomenon in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), referring to a deliberately partial or delayed resuscitation attempt in patients with poor prognosis or terminal conditions. Although it is recognized in clinical practice, the concept remains ambiguous and ethically controversial.
